target_customer: AI application companies and inference buyers that run open source LLMs and pay per token or for dedicated endpoints
problem: Serving open source models fast and cheaply on GPUs needs scarce kernel and performance engineering talent. Wafer uses AI agents as autonomous performance engineers that tune the whole serving stack to a customer's real traffic.
business_model: usage-based inference API (serverless per token) plus reserved and dedicated endpoints with SLAs
product_category: AI inference cloud and GPU kernel optimization

founders.name: Steven Arellano
education: University of Chicago, computer science and economics

competitors.name: Kernelize
competitors.what: Adjacent, not a direct rival: automates compiler backends for AI accelerators on the open source Triton project, launched by Open Core Ventures
competitors.funding_then: Launched by Open Core Ventures; funding not stated in the launch post

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating kernel level tuning across GPUs and non Nvidia accelerators with agents is hard for a small team, though built on existing open source engines and models.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated kernel and tuning know how and hardware relationships help, but inference is a crowded commodity market where price is the main lever.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Reported acquisition offers from cloud and inference providers in 2026 were declined, according to press coverage.

market_need_then: Demand for cheaper inference on open models was rising in 2025 and GPU supply and kernel talent were constrained, pushing buyers to look for non Nvidia hardware and tuned stacks.

branding.domain_note: Uses wafer.ai; how it was obtained is not stated.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened
identity.visual_style: Minimal layout with ASCII and dot matrix graphics and a light and dark toggle, per its own site
identity.voice_and_tone: Short direct taglines such as Inference hyper-optimized for your workload

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct visual style on its own site, but no press or community evidence about the brand, and other companies share the Wafer name.

outcome_analysis: Wafer entered YC in Summer 2025 as a GPU kernel optimization company and by September 2026 announced a $40M Series A co-led by Marathon and Chemistry, with AMD Ventures participating. Press says it turned down acquisition offers. Growth came from the inference cost squeeze, non Nvidia hardware interest and a shift from kernel automation toward a full inference cloud.
notes: The Series A is sourced to Wing VC (investor post, September 2026) and cross-checked by a Wilson Sonsini announcement dated 2026-09-01. The $4M seed is now recorded: the company's own blog post by Emilio Andere dated 2026-04-14 and Menlo Times (dated Apr 16, year not shown on the page) both say 4 million led by Fifty Years with Liquid2 and Y Combinator participating. A Dealroom news item with a matching headline could not be opened (rate limited), so the confirmation is the company post plus Menlo Times. Valuation above $200M appears only in secondary outlets (Crypto Briefing, KuCoin flash) and is not recorded; Employbl lists a conflicting $800K pre-seed, also not recorded. The company was previously listed as Herdora on YC and aggregator pages; one aggregator gives founding year 2023. Competitor search near the Summer 2025 batch found only Kernelize (launch post 2025-05-01), listed as adjacent because it targets Triton compiler backends and not kernel tuning agents. Other GPU kernel agent companies found (Standard Kernel, Makora, RightNow AI) had no source dated near the batch, so they are not listed. Standard Kernel is a separate company.
